key_insight: The paper shows that quantum circuit training performance depends strongly on how search directions and parameter-update rules are combined, not just on the optimizer name itself.
engineering_relevance: Its modular benchmark helps practitioners choose optimization strategies for QAOA, QML, QCNN, and VQE under limited shots, constrained evaluation budgets, and hardware noise.
method: Separated quantum search-direction estimation from classical update rules to benchmark them independently.
Compared gradient-based, stochastic, and derivative-free optimizers across QAOA, Iris classification, QCNN on binary MNIST, and VQE for H2.
Tested under finite-shot simulation and on a 156-qubit processor, tracking objective values and evaluation costs.
evidence_signal: The study reports terminal and best objectives, post-training accuracies, and peak/mean results across three seeds for simulator runs, plus selected trajectories for MaxCut and hydrogen.
watch_item: The hardware experiments do not establish a ranking among optimizers and do not isolate a causal effect of device noise.
paper_title: Benchmarking Modular Optimization Strategies for Parameterized Quantum Circuits
